Lauren / team — quick answers from infra side:

1) IP ranges: For private deployments we publish a small set of egress CIDR ranges per-region. For US regions the control plane & telemetry use: 34.210.120.0/22 and 52.14.200.0/23. Those are the addresses our support/control plane will use for callbacks and telemetry; customer egress can NAT these to an allowlist.

2) Ports/protocols:
- Outbound TCP 443 (HTTPS) required for control plane, updates, and telemetry.
- Outbound TCP 443 to model artifact endpoints (S3-compatible) and optional model download acceleration.
- Optional: TCP 22 only for scheduled on-prem maintenance when customer explicitly enables it (we do not request it by default).
- No other ports are required for normal token inference traffic.

3) Inbound public IPs: Not required. Private deployment operates outbound-only from the customer VPC to the control plane. We do not open inbound holes to the internet on customer networks. Management/agent connections are initiated outbound and authenticated with mutually verified TLS certs.

4) KMS/HSM endpoints: We integrate with customer KMS in a customer-managed mode. We do not need firewall rules to your KMS unless you choose Redwood-managed keys; in that case we will provide the specific endpoints. Telemetry endpoints are inside our control plane CIDRs above.

Proxy/NAT: Compatible with HTTP proxies and NAT. If your egress is intercepted, ensure TLS passthrough for 443 so mutual TLS certs are validated.

Attachment: redwood-vpc-egress-checklist.xlsx (local infra reference)

Adding the security perspective:

- We can provide a short attestation and SOC-related answers; attached is our current SOC-2 excerpt and the standard network controls doc we share for private deployments. I included recommended TLS cipher suites and a note that we require certificate pinning for mutual-auth flows.
- Telemetry: Only minimal operational telemetry is sent (metrics/health). Customers can opt-out of application-level telemetry; control-plane telemetry is needed for platform health and SLA.
- IP allowlist maintenance: We publish a stable CIDR bundle and a signed manifest (via Drive link/JIRA) at least 30 days before changes. For customers with strict change windows we can request a managed change freeze.
- Audit/logging: We produce audit logs for model requests and admin actions; we can route logs to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder if required.

Joe — thanks for the quick list. See consolidated answers below (short form for your auditors). If you want we can follow with a 30m screen share to walk the checklist.

1) Egress/control-plane IP ranges (US): 34.210.120.0/22, 52.14.200.0/23. We will provide a signed CIDR manifest and maintain a 30-day notification window before changes. If you need contract-level guarantees, Marcus can propose a Dedicated egress block as an add-on.

2) Ports/protocols: Outbound TCP 443 (HTTPS) only. Optional TCP 22 only when explicitly enabled for scheduled maintenance. No inbound public IPs are required.

3) Inbound requirement: None. All management/control plane connections are outbound from your VPC. We authenticate using mutual TLS and certificate pinning. Ensure TLS passthrough if you terminate TLS at a proxy.

4) KMS/HSM/telemetry: We integrate with customer-managed KMS; no external KMS endpoints need to be whitelisted unless you request Redwood-managed keys (in which case we'll provide endpoints). Telemetry is minimal; customers may opt out of application-level telemetry.
